tagline: North out of Grand Rapids, lake after lake.
intro: Grand Rapids is named for rapids on the Mississippi that now lie hidden under a paper-company dam. Out of town Highway 38 heads north 47 miles to Effie, a twisty road over rolling hills and past bogs, through the resort lakes and into the Chippewa National Forest, which holds more lakes and wetlands than any other national forest in the country.
Voyageurs and loggers came this way first. The highway was authorized in 1933 and paved all the way by 1940, and Marcell and Bigfork both grew up as stops on the Minneapolis and Rainy River Railway.

moments.title: Forest History Center
moments.text: Costumed interpreters keep a logging camp of 1900 by the Mississippi, with a floating cook shack moored at the river and a 100-foot CCC fire tower anyone over six may climb.

moments.title: Marcell
moments.text: Founded as Turtle Lake in 1905 and renamed the next year, the old name being taken, for a railway conductor who had an accident nearby.

moments.title: Scenic State Park
moments.text: Seven miles east of Bigfork, virgin pine stands around Sandwick and Coon lakes, beside log buildings raised by the state's first CCC park camp.
